description: Synthetic golden cases for A2 English writing assessment. All text is invented for testing purposes.

cases.input: Yesterday I go to the park with my friend. We play football for two hours.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: Yesterday I went to the park with my friend. We played football for two hours.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good attempt at describing a past event. Remember to use past tense verbs when talking about yesterday.

errors.explanation: Use past tense 'went' for actions completed yesterday.
Use past tense 'played' for completed past actions.

tips: Use time markers like 'yesterday' with past tense

cases.input: My brother don't like vegetables. He prefer meat and potatoes.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My brother doesn't like vegetables. He prefers meat and potatoes.
referenceResponse.feedback: Subject-verb agreement needs attention. Third person singular requires 'doesn't' and verbs ending in -s.

errors.explanation: Use 'doesn't' with third person singular (he/she/it).
Add -s to verbs with third person singular subjects.

cases.input: I need a book. Can you give me book about history?

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I need a book. Can you give me a book about history?
referenceResponse.feedback: Articles (a/an/the) are important. Use 'a' before singular countable nouns when mentioning them for the first time.

errors.explanation: Use 'a' before singular countable nouns mentioned for the first time.

cases.input: I have two cat and three dog at home.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I have two cats and three dogs at home.
referenceResponse.feedback: Remember to use plural forms after numbers greater than one.

errors.explanation: Use plural 'cats' after 'two'.
Use plural 'dogs' after 'three'.

tips: Always use plural nouns after numbers > 1

cases.input: The meeting is at Monday at 3pm.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The meeting is on Monday at 3pm.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use 'on' with days of the week, not 'at'.

errors.explanation: Use 'on' before days of the week.

tips: Use 'on' with days: on Monday, on Friday
Use 'at' with times: at 3pm, at noon

cases.input: She very happy yesterday because she pass the exam.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: She was very happy yesterday because she passed the exam.
referenceResponse.feedback: Missing verb 'was' and past tense 'passed'. Remember complete sentences need a verb.

errors.explanation: Include the verb 'was' for past tense descriptions.
Use past tense 'passed' for completed actions.

tips: Use past tense for completed events

cases.input: I interested in learning English. It is very useful for my job.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I am interested in learning English. It is very useful for my job.
referenceResponse.feedback: Missing verb 'am'. Use 'I am interested' not 'I interested'.

errors.explanation: Include the verb 'am' with adjectives like 'interested'.

tips: Always include the verb 'be' with adjectives
Practice: I am happy, She is tired

cases.input: My favorite color are blue. I like blue sky and ocean.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My favorite color is blue. I like the blue sky and ocean.
referenceResponse.feedback: Subject-verb agreement: 'color' is singular, so use 'is' not 'are'.

errors.explanation: Use 'is' with singular subjects like 'color'.

cases.input: We goes to school every day. My friends goes too.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: We go to school every day. My friends go too.
referenceResponse.feedback: Subject-verb agreement: 'we' and 'friends' are plural, so use 'go' not 'goes'.

errors.explanation: Use 'go' with plural subjects (we, they, friends).
Use 'go' with plural subjects (we, they, friends).

cases.input: I want buy a new phone. It cost too much money.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I want to buy a new phone. It costs too much money.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use 'to' after 'want' before another verb. Also, 'it' requires 'costs' (third person singular).

errors.explanation: Use 'want to + verb' structure.
Add -s for third person singular (it/he/she).

cases.input: There is many people in the park today.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: There are many people in the park today.
referenceResponse.feedback: 'People' is plural, so use 'are' not 'is'.

errors.explanation: Use 'are' with plural nouns like 'people'.

cases.input: She don't has any brothers. She have only one sister.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: She doesn't have any brothers. She has only one sister.
referenceResponse.feedback: Negative form: 'doesn't have' (not 'don't has'). Positive: 'she has' (not 'she have').

errors.explanation: Use 'doesn't have' for negative with third person singular.
Use 'has' with third person singular (she/he/it).

cases.input: I usually wake up at 7 oclock in the morning.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I usually wake up at 7 o'clock in the morning.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good sentence structure. Just remember the apostrophe in 'o'clock'.

errors.explanation: Use apostrophe: o'clock (of the clock).

cases.input: My house is near the school. I walk there everyday.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My house is near the school. I walk there every day.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good! Just note: 'every day' (two words) means each day. 'Everyday' (one word) is an adjective meaning ordinary.

errors.explanation: 'Every day' (two words) = each day. 'Everyday' (one word) = ordinary.

cases.input: He can speaks three languages: English, Spanish, and French.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: He can speak three languages: English, Spanish, and French.
referenceResponse.feedback: After modal verbs (can, could, will, etc.), use the base form without -s.

errors.explanation: Use base form after 'can': can speak (not can speaks).

tips: Modal + base verb: can go, will eat, should study

cases.input: I am study English for two years now.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I have been studying English for two years now.
referenceResponse.feedback: For actions that started in the past and continue now, use present perfect continuous: 'have been studying'.

errors.explanation: Use present perfect continuous for ongoing actions: have been + verb-ing.

tips: Present perfect continuous: have/has been + verb-ing
Use for actions continuing from past to now

cases.input: The weather is very hot today. I think I will go swim in the pool.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The weather is very hot today. I think I will go swimming in the pool.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good! Use 'go swimming' (go + verb-ing) for activities.

errors.explanation: Use 'go + verb-ing' for activities: go swimming, go running, go shopping.

tips: Go + activity-ing: go swimming, go shopping

cases.input: My mother cook dinner every evening. She is very good chef.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My mother cooks dinner every evening. She is a very good chef.
referenceResponse.feedback: Third person singular needs -s (cooks). Also, use 'a' before singular nouns (a chef).

errors.explanation: Add -s for third person singular (she/he/it).
Use 'a' before singular countable nouns.

cases.input: I dont like cold weather. I prefer hot climate.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I don't like cold weather. I prefer a hot climate.
referenceResponse.feedback: Remember the apostrophe in 'don't'. Also, use 'a' before singular countable nouns.

errors.explanation: Use apostrophe in contractions: don't, can't, won't.
Use 'a' before singular countable nouns.

tips: Use articles with singular countable nouns

cases.input: Last summer we travel to Italy. The food was delicious and the people was friendly.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: Last summer we traveled to Italy. The food was delicious and the people were friendly.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use past tense for completed events. 'People' is plural, so use 'were'.

errors.explanation: Use past tense for completed past events.
'People' is plural, use 'were' not 'was'.

cases.input: I have a dog. His name is Max. He like to play in the park.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I have a dog. His name is Max. He likes to play in the park.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good sentence structure! Just remember third person singular: 'he likes' (not 'he like').

errors.explanation: Add -s for third person singular (he/she/it).

tips: Practice with animals: The cat sleeps, The bird sings

cases.input: She is teacher at my school. She teach mathematics.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: She is a teacher at my school. She teaches mathematics.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use 'a' before singular professions. Also, 'she teaches' (not 'she teach').

errors.explanation: Use 'a' before singular countable nouns (professions).
Add -es for third person singular with verbs ending in -ch.

tips: Use articles with professions: a teacher, a doctor

cases.input: We was very tired after the long journey. But we enjoy the trip.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: We were very tired after the long journey. But we enjoyed the trip.
referenceResponse.feedback: 'We' requires 'were' (not 'was'). Use past tense 'enjoyed' for completed events.

errors.explanation: Use 'were' with we/you/they.
Use past tense for completed past events.

cases.input: My favorite food are pizza and pasta. I eat they every week.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My favorite food is pizza and pasta. I eat them every week.
referenceResponse.feedback: 'Food' is singular (use 'is'). Use object pronoun 'them' after verbs.

errors.explanation: 'Food' is singular, use 'is'.
Use object pronoun 'them' after verbs.

tips: Subject pronouns: I, you, he, she, they
Object pronouns: me, you, him, her, them

cases.input: I am very interesting in learning new languages. It is important for my career.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I am very interested in learning new languages. It is important for my career.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use 'interested' (feeling) not 'interesting' (describing something). 'I am interested' = I feel interest.

errors.explanation: 'Interested' describes feelings. 'Interesting' describes things.

cases.input: The childrens are playing in the garden. They is very happy.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The children are playing in the garden. They are very happy.
referenceResponse.feedback: 'Children' is already plural (no -s needed). Use 'are' with 'they'.

errors.explanation: 'Children' is the plural of 'child' (irregular plural).
Use 'are' with plural subjects (they).

cases.input: I need to practice more. My English is not very good yet.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I need to practice more. My English is not very good yet.
referenceResponse.feedback: Excellent! Your sentences are grammatically correct and clear. Keep practicing!

cases.input: She dont likes coffee. She prefer tea with milk.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: She doesn't like coffee. She prefers tea with milk.
referenceResponse.feedback: Negative: 'doesn't like' (not 'dont likes'). Positive: 'she prefers' (add -s).

errors.explanation: Negative: doesn't + base verb (no -s).
Third person singular needs -s.

cases.input: I have two brothers. They both study at university.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I have two brothers. They both study at university.
referenceResponse.feedback: Perfect! Clear, correct sentences with good grammar.
tips: Try using more adjectives to describe

cases.input: The book is very interest. I read it last week.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The book is very interesting. I read it last week.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use adjective 'interesting' to describe things. 'Interest' is a noun or verb.

errors.explanation: Use adjective form: interesting (not noun 'interest').

cases.input: We goes to the beach every summer. The water is always cold.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: We go to the beach every summer. The water is always cold.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good! Just remember: 'we go' (not 'we goes'). Use base form with we/you/they.

errors.explanation: Use base form with plural subjects: we go, they go.

cases.input: My sister want to become a doctor. She study very hard every day.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My sister wants to become a doctor. She studies very hard every day.
referenceResponse.feedback: Third person singular needs -s: 'wants' and 'studies'.

errors.explanation: Add -s for third person singular.
Verbs ending in -y change to -ies: study-studies.

cases.input: I am looking for a job. Do you know any company that hire new employees?

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I am looking for a job. Do you know any company that hires new employees?
referenceResponse.feedback: Good question structure! 'Company' is singular, so use 'hires'.

errors.explanation: Singular subject 'company' needs 'hires'.

cases.input: The movie was very bored. I sleep during the film.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The movie was very boring. I slept during the film.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use 'boring' to describe things. Use past tense 'slept' for completed events.

errors.explanation: 'Boring' describes things. 'Bored' describes feelings.
Use past tense for completed past events.

cases.input: There is a lot of traffic today. The cars move very slow.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: There is a lot of traffic today. The cars move very slowly.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use adverb 'slowly' to describe how something happens (verb + adverb).

errors.explanation: Use adverb form to modify verbs: move slowly.

cases.input: I usually have breakfast at 8 am. Then I go to work by bus.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I usually have breakfast at 8 am. Then I go to work by bus.
referenceResponse.feedback: Excellent! Perfect grammar and clear sequence of actions.
tips: Keep using time markers: usually, then, after that

cases.input: He can to play the guitar very well. He practice every day.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: He can play the guitar very well. He practices every day.
referenceResponse.feedback: After 'can', use base verb without 'to'. Also, 'he practices' (third person singular).

errors.explanation: Modal verbs (can, will, should) + base verb (no 'to').
Add -s for third person singular.

cases.input: My parents lives in a small town. They has a nice house there.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My parents live in a small town. They have a nice house there.
referenceResponse.feedback: 'Parents' is plural, so use 'live' and 'have' (not 'lives' and 'has').

errors.explanation: Plural subjects use base form: they live.
Plural subjects use 'have': they have.

cases.input: I am very tired today. I didnt sleep well last night.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I am very tired today. I didn't sleep well last night.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good! Just remember the apostrophe in 'didn't'.

errors.explanation: Use apostrophe in contractions: didn't, wasn't, couldn't.

tips: Common contractions: don't, can't, won't, didn't

cases.input: She is more taller than her sister. They are both very tall.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: She is taller than her sister. They are both very tall.
referenceResponse.feedback: For short adjectives, use -er (taller), not 'more taller'.

errors.explanation: Short adjectives: add -er (tall-taller). Don't use 'more' with -er.

cases.input: I have been to Paris last year. It was beautiful city.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I went to Paris last year. It was a beautiful city.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use simple past 'went' with specific time (last year). Use 'a' before singular nouns.

errors.explanation: Use simple past with specific past time: last year, yesterday.
Use 'a' before singular countable nouns.

cases.input: The test was very difficult. Many students dont pass it.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The test was very difficult. Many students didn't pass it.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use past tense 'didn't pass' for completed events. Also, remember the apostrophe.

errors.explanation: Use apostrophe in contractions.
Use past tense for completed past events.

cases.input: I like to read book before bed. It help me relax.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I like to read books before bed. It helps me relax.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use plural 'books' for general statements. 'It helps' (third person singular).

errors.explanation: Use plural for general statements about activities.
Third person singular needs -s: it helps.

tips: General activities: plural nouns (read books, watch movies)

cases.input: We was planning to go to the cinema, but we change our mind.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: We were planning to go to the cinema, but we changed our mind.
referenceResponse.feedback: 'We' requires 'were'. Use past tense 'changed' for completed events.

errors.explanation: Use 'were' with we/you/they.
Use past tense for completed past events.

cases.input: My best friend live in London. I visit him every summer.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: My best friend lives in London. I visit him every summer.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good! Just remember: 'friend' is singular, so 'lives' (not 'live').

errors.explanation: Third person singular needs -s: he/she/it lives.

tips: My friend lives, my friends live

cases.input: I am study for my exam next week. I need to review all the lessons.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I am studying for my exam next week. I need to review all the lessons.
referenceResponse.feedback: Use present continuous 'am studying' for current ongoing actions.

errors.explanation: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing.

cases.input: The restaurant serve delicious food. The waiter was very friendly.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: The restaurant serves delicious food. The waiter was very friendly.
referenceResponse.feedback: Good description! 'Restaurant' is singular, so 'serves' (not 'serve').

errors.explanation: Singular subjects need verb + s: the restaurant serves.

cases.input: I enjoy to watch movies on weekends. My favorite genre is comedy.

referenceResponse.corrected_text: I enjoy watching movies on weekends. My favorite genre is comedy.
referenceResponse.feedback: After 'enjoy', use verb-ing (enjoy watching), not 'to + verb'.

errors.explanation: Verbs like enjoy, love, hate + verb-ing.

tips: I enjoy reading, She loves dancing
